display.purpose: The single page title per route, always paired with a muted subtitle.

title.purpose: Dialog titles. Line-height 1 because a dialog title labels the dialog.

body.purpose: The default for table cells, menu items, descriptions and helper text.

label.purpose: Form labels, button text, sidebar items, and the subject column of a table.

micro.purpose: Uppercase table column headers. The system's one micro-typographic signature.

shadows.name: seat
shadows.purpose: Sub-perceptual seat under inputs, checkboxes and outline buttons. Part of the hairline tier, not a depth step.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: The active tab pill. The only in-page shadow, and it marks a selected state rather than a container.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and sheets — the top layer of the app, always over a 50% black scrim.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Applies to every state transition.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover, focus and colour transitions on controls.

motion.name: duration-layer
motion.purpose: Dialog and sheet enter/exit (fade plus 95%-to-100% zoom), and sidebar width changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single main action on a screen. Its teal fill is one of the three sanctioned uses of the accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border: none; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.5982 0.10687 182.4689)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); font: 500 0.875rem/1.4286 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, oklch(0.5982 0.10687 182.4689)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The default for anything that is not the page's single main action: pagination, sort direction, theme toggle.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.922 0 0)); border-radius: 0.5rem; background: var(--background, oklch(1 0 0)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.145 0 0)); font: 500 0.875rem/1.4286 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.97 0 0)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Confirmation of a delete, revoke or archive. Alert Red is never used for status.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border: none; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)); color: #fff; font: 500 0.875rem/1.4286 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)) 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Transparent fill, hairline border, 36px tall. Focus moves the border to the ring colour and adds a 3px halo; only colour and box-shadow transition, so nothing reflows.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 2.25rem; width: 100%; min-width: 0; padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.922 0 0)); border-radius: 0.5rem; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.145 0 0)); font: 400 0.875rem/1.4286 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); outline: none; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.556 0 0)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)) 20%, transparent); }

components.name: Tag Chip
components.description: A value attached to a record. Fully round because pills mean data, not actions.
components.css: .ds-chip-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; width: fit-content; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--secondary, oklch(0.97 0 0)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(0.205 0 0)); font: 500 0.75rem/1.333 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }

components.name: Metadata Chip
components.description: A property of a record rather than an assignment: priority, recurrence rule. Reads lighter than the tag chip, which is correct.
components.html: Every week
components.css: .ds-chip-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; width: fit-content; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.922 0 0)); border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.145 0 0)); font: 500 0.75rem/1.333 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-outline svg { width: 0.75rem; height: 0.75rem; flex-shrink: 0; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Task Table
components.description: The signature component. Uppercase micro headers on a quiet fill, hairline row rules, muted supporting columns, and an italic muted phrase wherever a value is absent.

TitleProjectDue datePriority

components.css: .ds-table-wrap { position: relative; width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.922 0 0)); border-radius: 0.625rem; } .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font: 400 0.875rem/1.4286 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.145 0 0)); } .ds-table thead { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--muted, oklch(0.97 0 0)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-table th { height: 2.75rem; padding: 0 1rem; text-align: left; vertical-align: middle; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.556 0 0)); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.922 0 0)); } .ds-table td { padding: 0.75rem 1rem; vertical-align: middle; white-space: nowrap; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.922 0 0)); } .ds-table tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-table tbody tr { transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-table tbody tr:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--muted, oklch(0.97 0 0)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-cell-subject { font-weight: 500; } .ds-cell-done { text-decoration: line-through; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.556 0 0)); } .ds-cell-muted { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.556 0 0)); } .ds-cell-empty { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.556 0 0)); font-style: italic; }

components.name: Task Checkbox

components.css: .ds-check { display: inline-grid; place-content: center; width: 1rem; height: 1rem; margin-right: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.922 0 0)); border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); cursor: pointer; vertical-align: middle; transition: box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-check--on { background: var(--primary, oklch(0.5982 0.10687 182.4689)); border-color: var(--primary, oklch(0.5982 0.10687 182.4689)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); } .ds-check svg { width: 0.875rem; height: 0.875rem; } .ds-check:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring, oklch(0.708 0 0)) 50%, transparent); }

narrative.overview:
Taskly is a room full of instruments, not a poster. A person and their bots operate on the same tasks through the same records, and the interface's job is to keep those records legible and never to compete with them. Every surface is neutral grey or white; every control is a fixed-height, unshouting instrument; and exactly one colour — Signal Teal — is allowed to glow. When something on screen is teal, it is either the action to take, the place you are, or the field you are in. Nothing else earns it.

The character is precise, calm, and unobtrusive. Density is moderate: the page breathes at 24–32px between sections but stays tight inside a control, so a table of forty tasks reads as one continuous instrument rather than forty cards. Type is the system sans at four working sizes; there is no display face, no decorative weight, no ornament. Hierarchy comes from weight and colour temperature (ink versus muted ink), not from size jumps. The system is dual-theme by construction: light and dark are two calibrations of the same room, not two designs, and every token has a counterpart on the other side.

Depth is the one place the system is deliberately opinionated. Structure is built from ground, hairlines, and tonal steps; a real shadow is reserved for things that have genuinely left the page.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used sparingly: teal marks action, location, and focus — nothing else.
Neutral achromatic base (chroma 0) for every surface, border, and text tone.
Fixed control height of 36px (2.25rem) across buttons, inputs, and selects.
Tables are the primary content form; cards are not part of the shipped vocabulary.
10px base radius, stepping to 6px for small controls and full-round for badges.
Light and dark are mirrored calibrations, never independent designs.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal appears at most a few times per screen and always answers one of three questions: *what do I press*, *where am I*, or *what am I typing in*. A teal fill that answers none of those is decoration and must be removed. Status, category, priority, and tag are communicated with neutrals and shape — never by spending the accent.

rules.name: The Chroma Zero Rule
rules.body: Every structural token — surface, border, text, skeleton, divider — has chroma exactly `0`. There are no warm greys and no cool greys. If a neutral in this system carries chroma, it is a bug, not a mood.

rules.name: The Mirrored Theme Rule
rules.body: No colour may be introduced in one theme without its counterpart in the other, and the two are tuned for equal apparent weight rather than equal numeric lightness. The teal and the red both lighten in dark mode for exactly this reason.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Header Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with letter-spacing belongs to one job: labelling a band of rows. That covers table column headers and the group headers inside a list sheet — the dashboard's "Overdue" and "Due today" bands, and the "While you were away" band over its log. Both sit on the same `muted/50` fill, because they are the same device. It is the system's one micro-typographic signature and it holds only while nothing else borrows it: page headings, buttons, tabs, and badges are all sentence case.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: Text is 400 or 500 in the body of the interface; 600 and 700 are reserved for the four headline roles above. A third weight inside a table row or a form is noise.

rules.name: The 24-and-Done Rule
rules.body: Sections within a route are separated by 24px. Not 20, not 28, and not a second value introduced for one screen. If two blocks need to feel more related than that, nest them in a bordered container instead of shrinking the gap.

rules.name: The token split this depends on
rules.body: `--background` is the ground and `--card` is the sheet, and they are never interchangeable. Anything that should read as laid *on* the page takes `bg-card` — a table container, a filter bar, a settings panel, a dialog, an outline button. Only the page itself takes `bg-background`. Before this split both were pure white in light mode, so every sheet was white on white and held together by its border alone; the tone step is what makes the hairline tier legible.

rules.name: The Left-the-Page Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only on an element that has left the page plane: dialog, sheet, popover, dropdown, select, toast. Tables, filter bars, headers, sidebars, and content containers are flat and are separated by a hairline and a tonal step. A card-with-shadow is not a Taskly surface.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: Anything modal brings a `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)` overlay with it. A floating layer that traps focus must also visibly demote what it covers.

rules.name: The Pill-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Fully-round is reserved for badges — values attached to a record. If it is pressable and pill-shaped, it is miscommunicating.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every border in the system is 1px. Emphasis changes colour, never weight.

rules.name: The One Address Rule
rules.body: A record has exactly one place to be read and acted on: its panel. Rows carry no menu of their own, and there is no edit screen — the panel *is* the editor. Reading something must never mean opening four dialogs in turn, and changing a field must never mean opening a form that restates the record you are already looking at.

rules.name: No overflow menu
rules.body: There is no `⋮` anywhere on a record. A menu is what a surface reaches for when it has not decided where its actions belong, and every action here has a home: a field is changed in the field, a subtask is added from the Subtasks tab beneath the subtasks, and delete — the one act with no field and no undo — is a single destructive icon in the panel's corner, with no neighbours to mis-hit and no menu to open first.

rules.name: Edit in place, save per field
rules.body: Every property is its own control, and each one saves alone: a select the moment it changes, text when focus leaves it. The request carries only the field that moved. There is no Save button, so there is nothing to forget to press and nothing to discard; Escape returns a text field to its stored value. Success is silent — the value on screen is the receipt — and only a failure raises a toast.

rules.name: Controls rest flat
rules.body: A property list rendered as seven bordered inputs reads as a form to fill in; this is a record to read that happens to be editable. Each control drops its border and shadow at rest and takes `bg-accent` on hover, with the focus ring on `:focus-visible` as everywhere else. Fields the record cannot own — a subtask's project and schedule, which follow its parent — render as Ink Muted prose saying so, not as a disabled control.

rules.name: The Real Address Rule
rules.body: The open panel lives in the URL (`?task=<id>`), so it can be linked to and Back closes it. Every reference to a record anywhere in the product — an activity entry, a dashboard row, a breadcrumb — links to that record, never to the list it lives in. Dropping the reader on an unfiltered table and leaving them to find the thing again is a broken link that happens to return 200. The panel fetches by id rather than reading the loaded table, so a link still opens a record the current filters exclude.

rules.name: The Stay-Put Rule
rules.body: Opening a record never moves the reader to another screen. Every surface that lists tasks carries the panel's parameter and renders the panel itself, so the dashboard and the activity log open a task over themselves — a link out of a long log must not cost the reader their place in it. Links between records therefore target the current route, not a fixed one.

rules.name: Keep view state out of the query
rules.body: The open panel is view state, not a filter, so it must be stripped before the search object becomes an API query. Leaving it in puts it in the query key, and opening a record silently refetches the list behind the panel and flashes the whole page back to its skeleton.

dos: Spend Signal Teal on only three things: the primary action, the current location, and the focused field. See The One Signal Rule.
Keep every structural neutral at chroma `0`.
Separate in-page surfaces with a 1px hairline and a tonal step, and reserve shadows for layers that have left the page. See The Left-the-Page Rule.
Give every bordered container on the page `bg-card`. A bordered box left transparent inherits the ground and reads as an outline drawn on nothing.
Hold controls to the 36px height ladder (32 / 36 / 40) so a row of mixed buttons, inputs, and selects aligns without adjustment.
Use 24px between the sections of a route. See The 24-and-Done Rule.
Render an absent value as italic Ink Muted prose ("No due date"), never as an empty cell or an em dash.
Ship every loading state as a structural skeleton that matches the shape of the content it replaces — real column headers, realistic block widths.
Pair each page title with a one-line Ink Muted subtitle that says what the screen is for.
Define both theme values whenever a colour is added, tuned for equal apparent weight rather than equal lightness.
Give collapsed navigation items tooltips so the icon rail never costs a label.
donts: Introduce a second accent hue. Status, priority, and category are communicated with neutrals and shape.
Put a shadow on a table, filter bar, header, sidebar, or content container.
Reach for the `Card` component. The shipped container vocabulary is the bordered table and the bordered filter bar.
Use uppercase with letter-spacing for anything but a header over a band of rows. See The Uppercase-Header Rule.
Use a border wider than 1px. Emphasis changes the border's colour. See The One-Pixel Rule.
Make a pressable control fully round — pills mean data, not actions. See The Pill-Means-Data Rule.
Animate hover with lift, scale, or shadow. State changes are colour and ring only, at 150ms.
Add a font. The system stack carries every role, and that is the point of the North Star.

Reintroduce the FastAPI artwork in `public/assets/images`. The mark is now Taskly's own — the completion check on a Signal Teal tile, drawn inline in `Logo.tsx` so it follows the theme's primary token — and it appears on the authentication screens only; the app shell leads with the account, not the brand.
Swap `:focus-visible` for `:focus`. Focus rings appear for keyboard navigation, not on every mouse click.
